Its presence marks the `dependencies` directory as a Python package, making the modules within it importable as part of the `app.api.dependencies` namespace [[target/app/api/dependencies/__init__.py]].

`check_article_modification_permissions` is a FastAPI dependency function that enforces write-access control on an article [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::check_article_modification_permissions]]. It accepts two injected parameters: `current_article`, an `Article` resolved via `get_article_by_slug_from_path` [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::get_article_by_slug_from_path]], and `user`, a `User` resolved via `get_current_user_authorizer()` [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::get_current_user_authorizer]]. The function returns `None`, meaning it is used purely for its side effect as a guard [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::check_article_modification_permissions]]. It calls `check_user_can_modify_article` with the resolved article and user to determine whether the authenticated user has permission to modify the article [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::check_article_modification_permissions]]. If that check fails, the function raises an `HTTPException` with HTTP status `403 Forbidden` and a message indicating the user is not the author of the article [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::check_article_modification_permissions]].

`get_article_by_slug_from_path` is an asynchronous FastAPI dependency function that retrieves a single article by its URL slug [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::get_article_by_slug_from_path]].

It accepts three injected parameters: a `slug` string extracted from the request path (enforced to be at least one character long via `Path`), an optional `user` resolved by `get_current_user_authorizer(required=False)` so that unauthenticated callers are permitted, and an `articles_repo` of type `ArticlesRepository` supplied by `get_repository` [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::get_article_by_slug_from_path]] [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::get_current_user_authorizer]] [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::get_repository]].

The function delegates the actual database lookup to `articles_repo.get_article_by_slug`, passing both the slug and the resolved user so the repository can tailor the result to the caller's identity (for example, whether they follow the author) [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::get_article_by_slug_from_path]].

If the repository signals that no matching article exists by raising `EntityDoesNotExist`, the function catches that exception and re-raises an `HTTPException` with a `404 Not Found` status code [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::get_article_by_slug_from_path]].

On success it returns an `Article` instance to whichever route or downstream dependency declared it as a dependency [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::get_article_by_slug_from_path]].

`get_articles_filters` is a dependency function that collects query-string filter parameters for listing articles and packages them into a single structured object [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::get_articles_filters]]. It accepts five optional inputs: a `tag` string to filter by tag, an `author` string to filter by author username, and a `favorited` string to filter by the username of a user who favourited the articles — all three defaulting to `None` [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::get_articles_filters]]. The `limit` and `offset` parameters are integers bound through FastAPI's `Query`, meaning they are read directly from the HTTP query string; `limit` must be at least 1 and defaults to `DEFAULT_ARTICLES_LIMIT`, while `offset` must be at least 0 and defaults to `DEFAULT_ARTICLES_OFFSET` [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::get_articles_filters]]. The function constructs and returns an `ArticlesFilters` instance populated with all five values, giving callers a single typed object rather than a loose set of primitives [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::get_articles_filters]]. It raises no exceptions of its own, though FastAPI will automatically reject a request with a validation error if `limit` or `offset` fall outside their declared bounds [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py]].

This module serves as the collection of FastAPI dependency functions that mediate access to article resources — resolving filter parameters, looking up articles by URL slug, and enforcing write-access control [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py]].

The first dependency, `get_articles_filters`, handles listing queries by collecting up to five query-string parameters — `tag`, `author`, `favorited`, `limit`, and `offset` — and packaging them into a single typed `ArticlesFilters` object [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::get_articles_filters]]. The `limit` and `offset` values are read directly from the HTTP query string via FastAPI's `Query` binding, with `limit` enforced to be at least 1 and `offset` at least 0, so FastAPI itself will reject out-of-range values before the function body even runs [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::get_articles_filters]].

The second dependency, `get_article_by_slug_from_path`, is asynchronous and resolves a single `Article` from the URL path [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::get_article_by_slug_from_path]]. It injects the slug from the path, an optional authenticated user (so unauthenticated callers are permitted), and an `ArticlesRepository` instance, then delegates the database lookup to the repository, passing both the slug and the resolved user so that caller-specific details such as follow status can be reflected in the result [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::get_article_by_slug_from_path]]. If the repository raises `EntityDoesNotExist`, the function catches it and re-raises an `HTTPException` with a `404 Not Found` status code, translating a data-layer signal into a proper HTTP response [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::get_article_by_slug_from_path]].

The third dependency, `check_article_modification_permissions`, builds directly on `get_article_by_slug_from_path` by declaring it as its own injected dependency, meaning the article lookup is always performed before the permission check runs [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::check_article_modification_permissions]]. It also injects a fully authenticated `User` (authentication is required here, unlike in the lookup dependency) and passes both the article and the user to `check_user_can_modify_article` [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::check_article_modification_permissions]]. The function returns `None` and is used purely for its side effect: if the authenticated user is not the article's author, it raises an `HTTPException` with a `403 Forbidden` status, halting the request before the route handler is reached [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::check_article_modification_permissions]].

Taken together, the three functions form a layered chain: filters are resolved independently for list endpoints, slug lookup underpins both read and write paths, and the permission guard composes on top of the lookup to protect mutating operations [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py]].

`__call__` is an asynchronous method on the `RWAPIKeyHeader` class that acts as the entry point for API key extraction from an incoming HTTP request [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::RWAPIKeyHeader::__call__]]. It accepts a `requests.Request` object and returns an `Optional[str]`, which will be the extracted API key value if one is present [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::RWAPIKeyHeader::__call__]].

The method delegates the actual header-parsing logic entirely to the parent class by calling `super().__call__(request)` [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::RWAPIKeyHeader::__call__]]. Its sole added responsibility is to intercept any `StarletteHTTPException` raised by that parent call and re-raise it as a FastAPI `HTTPException`, substituting a project-defined authentication message for the original error detail [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::RWAPIKeyHeader::__call__]]. This translation ensures that authentication failures surface with a consistent, application-level error message rather than the generic Starlette default [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::RWAPIKeyHeader]].

The method is marked `async` and carries a `# noqa: WPS610` suppression comment, indicating that the linter would otherwise flag the `__call__` magic method definition, but it is intentionally permitted here as part of the FastAPI dependency-injection pattern [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::RWAPIKeyHeader::__call__]].

`RWAPIKeyHeader` is a class defined in [`target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py`](target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py) that extends FastAPI Security's `APIKeyHeader` base class [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::RWAPIKeyHeader]]. It is not a Pydantic model; it is a plain Python class that participates in FastAPI's dependency-injection system by inheriting from `APIKeyHeader` [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::RWAPIKeyHeader]].

The class declares no fields of its own, and because its parent is `APIKeyHeader` rather than a Pydantic `BaseModel`, there are no Pydantic-managed fields to describe [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::RWAPIKeyHeader]]. Its sole responsibility is to wrap the parent class's API-key extraction behaviour with application-specific error handling [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::RWAPIKeyHeader]].

The entire custom logic lives in a single asynchronous method, `__call__`, which accepts an incoming `requests.Request` and returns an `Optional[str]` representing the extracted key [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::RWAPIKeyHeader::__call__]]. Rather than re-implementing header parsing, `__call__` delegates entirely to the parent by calling `super().__call__(request)` [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::RWAPIKeyHeader::__call__]]. Its only addition is a `try`/`except` block that catches any `StarletteHTTPException` raised by the parent and re-raises it as a FastAPI `HTTPException`, replacing the original detail with a project-defined authentication message [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::RWAPIKeyHeader::__call__]]. This translation ensures that authentication failures surface with a consistent, application-level error message rather than the generic Starlette default [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::RWAPIKeyHeader]]. The method carries a `# noqa: WPS610` suppression comment because defining `__call__` as a magic method would otherwise be flagged by the linter, but it is intentionally permitted here as part of the FastAPI dependency-injection pattern [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::RWAPIKeyHeader::__call__]].

`_get_authorization_header` is a FastAPI dependency function that extracts and validates a JWT token from an incoming API key header [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_authorization_header]].

It accepts two injected parameters: `api_key`, a string pulled from the request via `Security(RWAPIKeyHeader(name=HEADER_KEY))`, and `settings`, an `AppSettings` instance provided by `Depends(get_app_settings)` [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_authorization_header]] [[target/app/core/config.py::get_app_settings]]. The function expects `api_key` to be a space-separated string of the form `"<prefix> <token>"`, and it splits this value using `api_key.split(" ")` to separate the two parts [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_authorization_header]].

If the split fails — meaning the header value does not contain a space and therefore cannot be unpacked into exactly two parts — the function raises an `HTTPException` with HTTP status `403 Forbidden` [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_authorization_header]]. It also raises a second `403 Forbidden` `HTTPException` if the extracted prefix does not match the expected `jwt_token_prefix` from application settings [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_authorization_header]] [[target/app/core/config.py::get_app_settings]]. In both error cases the detail message signals a wrong token prefix [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_authorization_header]].

When all checks pass, the function returns the raw token string — the second segment of the header value — for use by downstream dependencies or route handlers [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_authorization_header]].

`_get_authorization_header_optional` is a FastAPI dependency function that attempts to extract and validate an authorization header, but tolerates its absence gracefully [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_authorization_header_optional]].

It accepts two injected parameters: an optional `authorization` string retrieved via `Security(RWAPIKeyHeader(..., auto_error=False))`, which means FastAPI will not automatically raise an error if the header is missing, and an `AppSettings` instance supplied by `Depends(get_app_settings)` [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_authorization_header_optional]] [[target/app/core/config.py::get_app_settings]].

When an authorization value is present, the function delegates to the internal helper `_get_authorization_header`, passing along both the raw header value and the application settings, and returns whatever that helper produces [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_authorization_header_optional]]. If no authorization header was provided, the function returns an empty string rather than raising an exception, making it suitable for endpoints where authentication is optional [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_authorization_header_optional]]. The return type is declared as `str` in both cases [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_authorization_header_optional]].

`_get_authorization_header_retriever` is a factory function that selects and returns one of two authorization-header retrieval callables based on whether authentication is required [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_authorization_header_retriever]].

It accepts a single keyword-only parameter, `required`, which is a `bool` defaulting to `True` [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_authorization_header_retriever]]. When `required` is `True`, the function returns `_get_authorization_header`; when `False`, it returns `_get_authorization_header_optional` [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_authorization_header_retriever]]. Its declared return type is `Callable`, annotated with `# type: ignore` to suppress type-checker complaints about the unparameterised generic [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_authorization_header_retriever]].

The function carries no decorators and raises no exceptions of its own; it is a pure selector whose sole job is to hand the caller the appropriate retriever function depending on whether the authorization header is mandatory or optional [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_authorization_header_retriever]].

`_get_current_user` is an async FastAPI dependency function that resolves the currently authenticated user from a JWT token, returning a [`User`](target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py) object [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_current_user]].

It accepts three injected parameters: a `UsersRepository` instance supplied by `get_repository` [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::get_repository]], a raw JWT string extracted from the request's Authorization header by `_get_authorization_header_retriever` [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_authorization_header_retriever]], and an `AppSettings` instance that carries the application's secret key [[target/app/core/config.py::get_app_settings]].

The function first calls `jwt.get_username_from_token`, passing the token and the secret key obtained via `settings.secret_key.get_secret_value()` [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_current_user]]. If that call raises a `ValueError` — meaning the token is malformed or the signature is invalid — the function catches it and raises an `HTTPException` with HTTP 403 Forbidden [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_current_user]].

Once a username is successfully extracted, the function calls `users_repo.get_user_by_username` with that username [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_current_user]]. If no matching user exists in the database (an `EntityDoesNotExist` is raised), a second `HTTPException` with HTTP 403 Forbidden is raised, using the same malformed-payload detail message [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_current_user]]. Both failure paths deliberately return a 403 rather than 401 or 404, avoiding disclosure of whether the token or the user was the problem [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_current_user]].

`_get_current_user_optional` is an async dependency function that attempts to resolve the currently authenticated user when a token is optionally present, returning `None` instead of raising an error when no token is supplied [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_current_user_optional]].

It accepts three injected parameters via FastAPI's `Depends` mechanism: a `UsersRepository` instance sourced from `get_repository` [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::get_repository]], an optional authorization token string sourced from `_get_authorization_header_retriever` called with `required=False` [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_authorization_header_retriever]], and an `AppSettings` instance sourced from `get_app_settings` [[target/app/core/config.py::get_app_settings]].

When a token is present, the function delegates to the internal `_get_current_user` helper, passing the repository, token, and settings, and returns whatever that helper resolves — an `Optional[User]` [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_current_user_optional]]. When no token is present, it returns `None` immediately without attempting any lookup [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_current_user_optional]]. The key distinction from its non-optional counterpart is the use of `required=False` on the header retriever, which prevents an error from being raised on unauthenticated requests [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_authorization_header_retriever]].

`get_current_user_authorizer` is a factory function that returns one of two callables depending on whether authentication is mandatory for a given route [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::get_current_user_authorizer]]. It accepts a single keyword-only parameter, `required`, which is a boolean defaulting to `True` [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::get_current_user_authorizer]]. When `required` is `True`, it returns the stricter `_get_current_user` callable; when `False`, it returns `_get_current_user_optional`, which allows unauthenticated access [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::get_current_user_authorizer]]. The return type is annotated as `Callable`, suppressed from type-checking with a `# type: ignore` comment [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::get_current_user_authorizer]]. This pattern lets route handlers declare whether a valid current user is required or merely optional simply by passing the appropriate flag when wiring up their dependency [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py]].

This module is the central authentication layer for the API, responsible for extracting JWT tokens from incoming request headers, validating them, and resolving the authenticated user for use by route handlers [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py]].

The foundation is [`RWAPIKeyHeader`](target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::RWAPIKeyHeader), a subclass of FastAPI's `APIKeyHeader` that overrides `__call__` to intercept any `StarletteHTTPException` raised during header extraction and re-raises it as a FastAPI `HTTPException` carrying a consistent, application-defined authentication message [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::RWAPIKeyHeader]]. This translation ensures that all authentication failures surface with uniform error detail rather than the generic Starlette default [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::RWAPIKeyHeader]].

On top of that header extractor, two sibling dependency functions handle the raw Authorization header value itself. [`_get_authorization_header`](target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_authorization_header) uses `RWAPIKeyHeader` via `Security` to pull the header, splits it into a prefix and a token, and raises HTTP 403 if the header is malformed or if the prefix does not match the configured `jwt_token_prefix`, returning the raw token string on success [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_authorization_header]]. Its counterpart, [`_get_authorization_header_optional`](target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_authorization_header_optional), uses the same header source but with `auto_error=False`, meaning FastAPI will not raise automatically when the header is absent; when the header is present it delegates to `_get_authorization_header`, and when absent it returns an empty string rather than an error, making it safe for endpoints where authentication is not required [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_authorization_header_optional]].

The choice between those two header-extraction paths is mediated by [`_get_authorization_header_retriever`](target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_authorization_header_retriever), a factory function that accepts a keyword-only `required` boolean and returns `_get_authorization_header` when `True` or `_get_authorization_header_optional` when `False` [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_authorization_header_retriever]].

The raw token obtained from the header is then consumed by the user-resolution layer. [`_get_current_user`](target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_current_user) is an async dependency that calls `jwt.get_username_from_token` with the token and the application secret key, raising HTTP 403 on a malformed token, and then calls `users_repo.get_user_by_username` to fetch the domain `User`, raising another HTTP 403 if no matching record exists [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_current_user]]. Both failure paths use the same 403 status and malformed-payload detail, deliberately avoiding disclosure of whether the token or the user account was the problem [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_current_user]]. Its optional counterpart, [`_get_current_user_optional`](target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_current_user_optional), wires `_get_authorization_header_retriever` with `required=False` so that an absent token causes an immediate `None` return rather than an error, delegating to `_get_current_user` only when a token is actually present [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::_get_current_user_optional]].

The single public entry point for route handlers is [`get_current_user_authorizer`](target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::get_current_user_authorizer), a factory function that mirrors the same `required` boolean pattern: passing `True` (the default) returns `_get_current_user`, while passing `False` returns `_get_current_user_optional`, allowing any route to declare whether a valid authenticated user is mandatory or merely optional simply by choosing the appropriate flag when wiring up its dependency [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::get_current_user_authorizer]].

`check_comment_modification_permissions` is a FastAPI dependency function that enforces authorization on comment mutation operations [[target/app/api/dependencies/comments.py::check_comment_modification_permissions]]. It accepts two injected arguments: a `Comment` instance resolved by `get_comment_by_id_from_path` and a `User` instance resolved by `get_current_user_authorizer`, both wired through FastAPI's `Depends` mechanism [[target/app/api/dependencies/comments.py::get_comment_by_id_from_path]] [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::get_current_user_authorizer]]. The function returns `None`, meaning it is used purely for its side effect as a guard rather than to supply a value to the route [[target/app/api/dependencies/comments.py::check_comment_modification_permissions]]. It delegates the actual ownership check to `check_user_can_modify_comment`, passing in the resolved comment and user [[target/app/api/dependencies/comments.py::check_comment_modification_permissions]]. If that check fails — indicating the authenticated user is not the author of the comment — the function raises an `HTTPException` with HTTP 403 Forbidden, preventing the request from proceeding [[target/app/api/dependencies/comments.py::check_comment_modification_permissions]].

`get_comment_by_id_from_path` is an asynchronous FastAPI dependency function that retrieves a single comment by its numeric ID within the context of a specific article [[target/app/api/dependencies/comments.py::get_comment_by_id_from_path]].

It accepts four injected parameters: `comment_id`, an integer path parameter constrained to be greater than or equal to 1; `article`, resolved by delegating to `get_article_by_slug_from_path`; an optional `user`, resolved via `get_current_user_authorizer` with `required=False` so unauthenticated callers are permitted; and `comments_repo`, a `CommentsRepository` instance obtained from the database layer [[target/app/api/dependencies/comments.py::get_comment_by_id_from_path]] [[target/app/api/dependencies/articles.py::get_article_by_slug_from_path]] [[target/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py::get_current_user_authorizer]] [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::get_repository]].

The function delegates the actual lookup to `comments_repo.get_comment_by_id`, passing the resolved `comment_id`, `article`, and `user`, and returns the resulting `Comment` on success [[target/app/api/dependencies/comments.py::get_comment_by_id_from_path]].

If the repository signals that no matching comment exists by raising `EntityDoesNotExist`, the function catches that exception and re-raises an `HTTPException` with a `404 Not Found` status code [[target/app/api/dependencies/comments.py::get_comment_by_id_from_path]].

This module serves as the dependency layer for comment-related route operations, providing FastAPI dependencies that handle both comment retrieval and authorization enforcement [[target/app/api/dependencies/comments.py]].

The first function, `get_comment_by_id_from_path`, is an asynchronous dependency responsible for resolving a comment from the current HTTP request context [[target/app/api/dependencies/comments.py::get_comment_by_id_from_path]]. It collects four injected inputs: a numeric path parameter `comment_id` (constrained to be at least 1), an `Article` resolved from the URL slug, an optional `User` that may be absent for unauthenticated requests, and a `CommentsRepository` wired in from the database layer [[target/app/api/dependencies/comments.py::get_comment_by_id_from_path]]. It forwards all three context values to the repository's lookup method and returns the resulting `Comment` on success [[target/app/api/dependencies/comments.py::get_comment_by_id_from_path]]. When no matching comment exists, it converts the repository's `EntityDoesNotExist` signal into an `HTTPException` with a 404 status code, translating a data-layer concern into a proper HTTP response [[target/app/api/dependencies/comments.py::get_comment_by_id_from_path]].

The second function, `check_comment_modification_permissions`, builds directly on the first by consuming `get_comment_by_id_from_path` as one of its own injected dependencies [[target/app/api/dependencies/comments.py::check_comment_modification_permissions]]. It also requires an authenticated `User`, making authentication mandatory rather than optional at this stage [[target/app/api/dependencies/comments.py::check_comment_modification_permissions]]. The function returns `None` and is used purely as a guard: it delegates the ownership check to `check_user_can_modify_comment`, and if that check fails it raises an `HTTPException` with HTTP 403 Forbidden, blocking the route from executing [[target/app/api/dependencies/comments.py::check_comment_modification_permissions]]. Together the two functions form a layered chain — lookup first, authorization second — so that any route needing protected write access to a comment can declare `check_comment_modification_permissions` as a single dependency and receive both behaviours automatically [[target/app/api/dependencies/comments.py::get_comment_by_id_from_path]] [[target/app/api/dependencies/comments.py::check_comment_modification_permissions]].

`_get_connection_from_pool` is an asynchronous generator function defined in [`target/app/api/dependencies/database.py`](target/app/api/dependencies/database.py) that borrows a single database connection from a connection pool and makes it available for the duration of a request [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::_get_connection_from_pool]].

It accepts one parameter, `pool`, a `Pool` instance that is resolved automatically via FastAPI's dependency injection using `Depends(_get_db_pool)`, meaning the pool itself is obtained by calling `_get_db_pool` before this function runs [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::_get_db_pool]] [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::_get_connection_from_pool]]. The function returns an `AsyncGenerator[Connection, None]`, so rather than returning a bare value it `yield`s a connection inside an `async with` block, which guarantees the connection is released back to the pool once the caller is finished with it [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::_get_connection_from_pool]].

Internally it calls `pool.acquire()` as an async context manager; the acquired `Connection` object is what gets yielded to whatever FastAPI route or downstream dependency injects this function [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::_get_connection_from_pool]]. Because the yield sits inside the `async with` block, teardown — returning the connection to the pool — happens automatically after the dependent code completes, whether it succeeds or raises an exception [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::_get_connection_from_pool]].

`_get_db_pool` is a small accessor function that takes a single argument — `request`, typed as `Request` — and returns a `Pool` [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::_get_db_pool]]. Its sole job is to retrieve the database connection pool that was attached to the application at startup, reading it from `request.app.state.pool` and returning it directly to the caller [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::_get_db_pool]]. It performs no validation, no I/O, and raises no exceptions of its own [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py::_get_db_pool]]. Because it accepts a `Request` object and returns a `Pool`, it is shaped for use as a FastAPI dependency — other route handlers or dependencies can declare it as a dependency to receive the shared pool without knowing where it lives [[target/app/api/dependencies/database.py]].
